kept.claim: TestLogger.FromContext returns a brand-new TestLogger, so any log written through FromContext (as LoggerMiddleware now does) is invisible to the test that holds the original TestLogger.
kept.body:
## [ISSUE] `TestLogger.FromContext` discards everything logged through it

**Severity:** LOW — test-only, but it makes the new logging path in `LoggerMiddleware` untestable with the existing fake.

### The Problem

```go
func (f *TestLogger) FromContext(_ context.Context) Logger {
	return NewTestLogger()
}
```

Every call returns a fresh `TestLogger` with its own zeroed `DebugLogs`/`InfoLogs`/`WarnLogs`/`ErrorLogs`. The test that built the logger keeps a pointer to the original, so it never sees those logs.

This PR moves `LoggerMiddleware` to log only through this path (`logger_middleware.go:58`):

```go
m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info("Plugin Request Completed", logParams...)
```

### Theory / Proof

`TestLogger` works by recording state on its receiver (`f.InfoLogs.Calls++`, etc. in `fake.go`). A method that hands back a different instance breaks that. Its sibling `New` (`fake.go:18-20`) has the same flaw, but nothing in the code under test called `New` on the logger it was given. `FromContext` is now called on every logged request.

### What happens today vs. what will break

Nothing breaks today because `LoggerMiddleware` has no test. The first test that passes `log.NewTestLogger()` to `NewLoggerMiddleware` and asserts `logger.InfoLogs.Calls == 1` will fail with 0 calls. The same happens to any existing test whose code under test later switches to `FromContext`. The fake then hides real behaviour instead of recording it.

### Research

The infra-level fake `pkg/infra/log/logtest/fake.go` is the pattern to copy: test fakes should record calls on the instance the test can see. testify-style spies return the receiver (or a child that shares state) for exactly this reason.

### Recommendation

Return the receiver so calls stay observable:

```go
func (f *TestLogger) FromContext(_ context.Context) Logger {
	return f
}
```
kept.evidence: pkg/plugins/log/fake.go:46-48: FromContext returns NewTestLogger(), a new zeroed struct, not the receiver f. After this PR, logger_middleware.go logs only through m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...), so a test that passes the fake to NewLoggerMiddleware would see InfoLogs.Calls == 0. No such test exists today, so this is a trap for future tests and LOW severity is right. New() at fake.go:18-20 and logtest/fake.go:66-68 follow the same pattern.

kept.claim: The new ContextualLoggerMiddleware and the rewritten LoggerMiddleware have no tests, so the fields dropped from the 'Plugin Request Completed' log line (pluginId, endpoint, dsName, dsUID, uname) are now guaranteed only by middleware ordering in CreateMiddlewares, and nothing checks that.
kept.body:
## [GAP ANALYSIS] Plugin request log fields now depend on untested middleware ordering

**Severity:** LOW — no bug today, but a reorder or a second middleware stack would silently drop `pluginId`/`endpoint`/`dsUID`/`uname` from the `grafana-data-egress` log.

### The Problem

Before this PR, `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` added `pluginId`, `endpoint`, `uname`, `traceID`, `dsName` and `dsUID` to its own log line. This PR removes them (`logger_middleware.go:49-58`) and relies on `ContextualLoggerMiddleware.instrumentContext` (this line) having put them in the context before `LoggerMiddleware` runs. That only holds because of the order in `pluginsintegration.go:158-161`:

```go
clientmiddleware.NewMetricsMiddleware(promRegisterer, registry),
clientmiddleware.NewContextualLoggerMiddleware(),
clientmiddleware.NewLoggerMiddleware(cfg, log.New("plugin.instrumentation")),
```

Neither middleware has a test file (`contextual_logger_middleware_test.go` / `logger_middleware_test.go` do not exist). The old instrumentation test never checked the contextual attributes either.

### Theory / Proof

`log.WithContextualAttributes` (`pkg/infra/log/log.go:285`) stores the params under `logParamsContextKey{}`. `ConcreteLogger.FromContext` (`log.go:203`) reads them only if a middleware *earlier* in the chain set them. `traceID` is now supplied by the provider registered in `tracing.ProvideService` (`pkg/infra/tracing/tracing.go:91`) rather than read directly. If `NewLoggerMiddleware` ends up above `NewContextualLoggerMiddleware`, or is reused in a stack without it, the egress log line goes out with only `status`, `duration`, `eventName` and `time_before_plugin_request`.

### What happens today vs. what will break

Today the order is right and the log line has the same fields as before, just in a different position. Swapping two lines in `CreateMiddlewares` would still compile and pass every test while removing the fields that log-based egress dashboards and alerts key on.

### Research

Other middlewares in this package ship with a `clienttest.NewClientDecoratorTest` test (e.g. `httpclient_middleware_test.go`, `metrics_middleware_test.go`), so the harness already exists.

### Recommendation

Add a test that chains both middlewares and checks the context the next client receives:

```go
func TestContextualLoggerMiddleware(t *testing.T) {
	cdt := clienttest.NewClientDecoratorTest(t, clienttest.WithMiddlewares(NewContextualLoggerMiddleware()))
	pCtx := backend.PluginContext{PluginID: "p", User: &backend.User{Login: "u"},
		DataSourceInstanceSettings: &backend.DataSourceInstanceSettings{Name: "n", UID: "uid"}}
	_, err := cdt.Decorator.QueryData(context.Background(), &backend.QueryDataRequest{PluginContext: pCtx})
	require.NoError(t, err)
	l := log.NewNopLogger().FromContext(cdt.QueryDataCtx)
	require.NotNil(t, l)
	// or assert on cdt.QueryDataCtx.Value via a small exported helper for the stored attributes
}
```

Also fix the order in place with a comment in `CreateMiddlewares`, e.g. `// must run before NewLoggerMiddleware: provides pluginId/endpoint/ds/user log attributes`.
kept.evidence: No *_test.go exists for contextual_logger_middleware.go or logger_middleware.go. The fields in the log line now depend on ConcreteLogger.FromContext (pkg/infra/log/log.go:203-217), the ctx-attributes provider (log.go:55-61) and the traceID provider (tracing.go:91-97). They appear only if ContextualLoggerMiddleware wraps LoggerMiddleware, which relies only on the order at pluginsintegration.go:158-161. No test or comment enforces that order.
